title: Allauddin v. State of U.P.
coram: Dilip Gupta, J.; Amar Singh Chauhan, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; competent authority to decide clause 6.5 dispute
headnote: A challenge to a Tehsildar recovery citation for electricity dues after disconnection is a factual dispute for clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The High Court disposed of the writ without deciding merits and directed the competent authority to examine and decide any such dispute expeditiously, preferably within six weeks.
facts: Allauddin challenged a citation dated 22 December 2015 issued by the Tehsildar Sadar, District Maharajganj, for recovery of electricity dues. He contended that the connection had been disconnected on 18 November 2010, so he could not be required to deposit those dues. Counsel for the Power Corporation stated that if a dispute were raised it would be decided in accordance with law expeditiously.

holding_units.holding: Whether electricity dues remain recoverable after disconnection is a factual dispute to be raised under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ court will not decide the claim on merits and will direct the competent authority to examine and decide any such dispute expeditiously in accordance with law.

not_decided.point: Whether electricity dues remained recoverable after disconnection on 18 November 2010
not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to adjudicate the merits of the petitioner's claim.
